steps.title: A wide valley
steps.body: South of Montélimar, the Rhône valley opens into a wide plain dotted with hills, around Avignon and Orange. The southern Rhône makes over 90% of all Rhône wine. Soils vary: large round stones, galets roulés, sand, clay and limestone. Côtes du Rhône covers the whole region.

steps.title: Mediterranean and windy
steps.body: The climate is Mediterranean: hot, dry summers, mild winters and plenty of sun. The Mistral, a cold, dry wind from the north, blows often, sometimes over 90 km/h. It dries vines after rain, reducing disease, and cools them, but can break shoots. Organic farming is common because conditions are healthy.

steps.prompt: How does the Mistral help vineyards?
options: It dries vines after rain, reducing disease
steps.explanation: A dry wind keeps grapes healthy.

steps.title: Popes and history
steps.body: In the 14th century, the popes moved to Avignon. They built a summer castle, the Châteauneuf-du-Pape, the pope's new castle, and planted vines. In 1923, Baron Le Roy of Châteauneuf drew up rules for the area's wine, which helped inspire France's AOC system, created in 1935.

steps.prompt: Châteauneuf-du-Pape's rules in the 1920s helped inspire the French AOC system.
steps.explanation: Yes. Baron Le Roy's 1923 rules were a model.

steps.title: What you learned
points: The southern Rhône makes over 90% of Rhône wine
Its Mediterranean climate and the Mistral keep vines healthy
The popes at Avignon gave Châteauneuf its name
